correctness.rationale: The source Appendix B proves even-sector nonnegativity with sole n=0 rotational null mode and that only the ground radial eigenfunction in each admissible odd sector can contribute. With H=1+(4k²−1)sin²x, independent symbolic differentiation confirmed for all symbolic positive integer k that L_{k,2k−1}(sin x)/sin x=[(2k−1)(2k+1)(4k−1)sin²x+8k²+4k−1]/H²>0. Dirichlet integration by parts makes E_{2k−1}[sin x]<0; all smaller positive odd n reduce n²/H and are negative. Independently checked L_{k,2k+1}(uplus)=0 where uplus=(1+(2k−1)sin²x)/√H is positive at endpoints, so weighted ground-state transform E_{2k+1}[f]=∫√(2H)uplus²|(f/uplus)′|²>0 for nonzero Dirichlet f, and higher odd n add positive potential. Exactly k negative odd frequencies have cosine and sine angular multiplicity two, giving index 2k; the only null is source n=0. This uses all-k algebra and genuine imported parity/nodal-domain theorems, not finite k experiments.
residual_risks: Relies on source Appendix B restriction of admissible Fourier parity and radial eigenfunction signs; not a full independent re-proof of source lemmas.
The positive profile uplus is not Dirichlet at endpoints; strict inequality follows exactly for Dirichlet f and must not be confused with a null state.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of index and nullity for the entire integer family of generalized Lawson bands removes the source’s all-k uncertainty and identifies the exact odd Fourier instability threshold. The result is structurally informative for minimal-surface stability rather than a tiny increment to known low-k computations.
residual_risks: Depends on original source mode-reduction theorem and is limited to generalized Dirichlet bands.

final_claim: For each integer k≥1 the generalized Lawson band has Dirichlet Morse index 2k and Dirichlet nullity 1; the admissible odd radial ground states are negative for n=1,3,…,2k−1 and positive for n≥2k+1.
limitations: Does not determine Morse index of closed Lawson surfaces or twisted families.
No numerical sampling is used as infinite proof; the main identities are symbolic all-k, while parity reduction is imported.
